questions.learningObjective: evaluate tracking adjustment in a design critique
questions.stem: On Tracking adjustment: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that all-capital words in a subhead look cramped together. Which global spacing change is most appropriate?

options.text: Increase the letter spacing uniformly across the subhead
Kern only the two most crowded letters in each word
options.misconception: treats a global spacing need as a pair-specific fix

options.text: Increase the size of the subhead without changing its spacing
options.misconception: confuses a change of scale with inter-letter spacing

options.text: Reduce the word spacing to compensate for the crowding
options.misconception: substitutes a different spacing dimension for the real fix

questions.explanation: Tracking, or letter spacing, adjusts the space between all characters in a range of text evenly. All-caps settings often need a small positive tracking value because capitals lack the natural spacing cues of lowercase, so a uniform increase is the right remedy.
questions.hint: Which adjustment applies to all the letters, not just one pair?

questions.learningObjective: evaluate line measure in a design critique
questions.stem: On Line measure: a designer reviewing a software company's landing page notices that body text runs so wide the eye loses its place at line endings. What is the most likely cause of this difficulty?

options.text: The measure of each line is too long for comfortable reading
The leading is far too generous for the chosen type size
options.misconception: blames vertical spacing for a horizontal reading problem

options.text: The text is set in a serif rather than a sans-serif face
options.misconception: incorrectly treats a type category as the underlying cause

options.text: The text is aligned left instead of being fully justified
options.misconception: mistakes the alignment choice for the length of each line

questions.explanation: Measure is the length of a line of text. When lines run too long, the eye has difficulty returning to the start of the next line, so a shorter measure improves reading comfort regardless of the typeface or the alignment that is used.
questions.hint: Think about how far the eye travels before it must jump back.
